title: Quokka Wellness — Chatbot Pilot Outreach & Objection Map
body:
Purpose:
- Quick internal scratch for outreach to Quokka Wellness (consumer mental health app).
- Goal: secure a 6-week technical pilot to evaluate Redwood Inference for an on-device/hosted hybrid chat assistant (triage + scheduling + micro-content).

Account snapshot: (from site + investor deck + LinkedIn)
- HQ: Austin, TX. Series B, ~120 employees, focus on B2C subscription mental health.
- CTO: Daniel Kim (eng org includes platform team + mobile).
- Product lead (behavioral health): Sara Liu (PM, previously at Calm).
- Current stack: iOS/Android app, Firebase, some serverless functions; in-house rule-based bot for intake.

Why they might care:
- Need to reduce costly human triage hours while keeping safety and quality.
- Looking for lower-latency local inference for offline flows + hosted fallbacks during peaks.
- Interested in quantization and cost savings vs few-shot API calls.

Pilot hypothesis (what we'll prove):
- Redwood can serve a safe triage funnel with 95% uptime and median response latency < 250ms (hosted+edge split).
- Unit cost per session 40-60% lower than current prompt-heavy vendor (estimate).
- Integration effort < 3 engineer-weeks using SDK + containerized private deployment for PII-sensitive flows.

Technical scope (MVP):
- Two user flows: initial intake (structured slot-fill), empathetic short-form responses, and scheduling handoff to calendar microservice.
- Module A: small edge model (quantized) for common Qs + intent classification (runs on-device or in private deploy).
- Module B: hosted larger model for fallback and follow-up generation.
- Logging + eval hooks: deterministic prompt versions + token cost dashboard in Redwood Console.

Outreach sequence (cold -> pilot ask):
1) Short intro email to Daniel (CTO): 2-3 lines, mention Redwood's hybrid routing + cost delta for chat-heavy workloads. Attach 1-page pilot plan.
2) Follow-up to Sara (PM): product angle, safety/guardrails examples, ask for design sync.
3) Technical follow-up: offer 30-min architecture review + free pilot credits.

Draft cold opener (email):
"Hi Daniel — quick note from Maya at Redwood. We help consumer health teams cut triage costs and keep response quality by routing requests between a small on-device model and a hosted fallback with per-route SLAs. I ran a quick estimate for a Quokka-like intake funnel and found potential token-cost savings of ~45% and median latency gains for common intents. If you have 20 minutes next week I can walk through a tailored 6-week pilot plan and a lightweight integration checklist. — Maya"

Objection map (anticipated + suggested reply):
- "We can't host anything with PII." -> "We can run the sensitive intake model in a private VPC or on-prem package; Redwood integrates with KMS/HSM for keys and supports audit logs. Pilot can start with non-PHI traffic to validate UX."
- "Latency is already good enough." -> "Fair — we can run side-by-side latency/cost A/B using Redwood's trace hooks and show per-route SLOs; often wins are on concurrent peaks and cost not median latency."
- "We don't want vendor lock." -> "Redwood's model catalog includes open variants and you can pin model versions; rollout policies allow easy fallback to your current infra while you evaluate."
- "We don't have ML infra bandwidth." -> "Offer solutions engineering time: 4 engineer-days from us for integration, plus templated SDK snippets and a demo app."

Metrics to propose for pilot success:
- Median response latency for common intents (target <250ms).
- Session completion rate (no handoff to human) delta.
- Cost per session compared to baseline.
- Safety regression checks (percentage of responses flagged by eval set).

Risks & mitigations:
- Data residency: use private deployment + customer-managed keys.
- Edge model drift: schedule weekly evals and auto-rollbacks from Redwood Console.
- Human-in-the-loop safety: configurable fallback threshold and routing policy to send ambiguous cases to human queue.

Next steps (internal):
- Ethan: pull telemetries or public error rates from similar customers (due 2026-01-14).
- Priya: draft 1-pager pilot plan + costs (due 2026-01-15).
- Maya: send intro email to Daniel + copy Sara (target 2026-01-13).

Notes to self / todo items:
- Prepare a short demo showing: 1) local quantized model on an Android emulator, 2) Redwood Console cost breakdown sample, 3) rollback to baseline.
- Create evaluation prompt set with 30 representative intake utterances (mix of PHI/adult/child phrasing).
- Pre-make security docs: sample SOC/ISO checklist snippets to send on request.

Loose brainstormed plays: 
- Offer a "concierge pilot" add-on where Redwood ops staff co-manage first 2 weeks of routing policies for higher confidence.
- Consider conversion pricing: discounts for committed Dedicated capacity if average throughput > X

Raw bits / shorthand (for later cleanup):
- possible value prop: "Reduce triage FTEs by X via deterministic routing + KV cache for repeated follow-ups"
- quick ask: 6-week pilot, 1-2 engs from Quokka, Redwood provides 4 SE days + credits

End of notes.
summary: Scratchpad for outbound to Quokka Wellness — pilot hypothesis, outreach scripts, objections + next steps
